newsitem.title: UK: Britain disturbed at Serbian crackdown threat.
newsitem.headline: Britain disturbed at Serbian crackdown threat.

text.p: Britain said on Monday it was disturbed by a Serbian government threat to crack down on opposition protests and urged it to respect democratic rights.

Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic raised the stakes in a two-week confrontation when police and city authorities warned on Sunday they would stop tolerating demonstrations in Belgrade that have drawn up to 100,000 protesters a day.
Britain's Foreign Office said it was disturbed that the Serbian interior ministry had issued a statement that the police had been more tolerant than required.
"We believe that the present situation requires the greatest restraint and tolerance on all sides and the avoidance of intemperate language which could further inflame the situation.
"We call on the Serbian authorities to continue to respect the democratic right of peaceful demonstration without qualification," the ministry said in a statement.
The demonstrations were sparked by the annulment of opposition victories in municipal polls on November 17.

The British foreign ministry said it was concerned at the political tension and had made strong representations about the annulment to Milosevic, a socialist who has ruled the former Yugoslav republic for nine years.
